subject: Request to add EdgeHarbor CDN as subprocessor — evidence & annex proposal
messages:
From: Michael Torres <michael@edgeharbor.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@edgeharbor.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request to add EdgeHarbor CDN as subprocessor (logs & caching)

Hi Karthik,

Following our intake last week, EdgeHarbor is preparing to onboard Redwood for a pilot that will route some anonymized telemetry through our CDN for edge caching and log distribution. Our security and procurement teams need formal confirmation that adding EdgeHarbor as a subprocessor is acceptable and a list of required evidence so we can complete our vendor review. Specifically they asked for:

- Confirmation of the flow-down DPA language (we need a signed Annex that binds EdgeHarbor to the same data obligations for EU data).
- SOC 2 attestation or equivalent plus any encryption-in-transit details.
- Commitment on 'no further subcontracting' clause (EdgeHarbor will need either a carve-in or a right to notify + 30-day objection window).

I've attached a short factsheet and SOC 2 summary. Can Redwood provide the DPA annex redlines you want us to sign and the list of evidence items procurement will accept? Also flag if any procurement timeline constraints (they're targeting contract close by 12/15).

Thanks —
Michael Torres
Head of Procurement, EdgeHarbor, Inc.
Attachments: EdgeHarbor_Security_Factsheet.pdf; EdgeHarbor_SOC2_Summary.docx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Michael Torres <michael@edgeharbor.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request to add EdgeHarbor CDN as subprocessor (logs & caching)

Hi Michael —

Thanks for the quick summary and the attachments. Appreciate the timeline — Redwood can move quickly here. I've looped in Kimberly (Legal) for the DPA/annex redlines and Jordan (Sales Ops) to coordinate procurement evidence.

High-level responses now:
- We can execute an Annex A (subprocessor flow-down) that mirrors our DPA obligations.
- For 'no further subcontracting' we generally require notice + approval for material subcontractors that touch unredacted customer content. For CDNs that only cache encrypted blobs, we have a standard notify+30-day objection approach.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II or equivalent, up-to-date pen test summary, TLS configuration notes, and a point of contact for security ops. We can accept a vendor attestation plus our own evidence intake.

Kimberly — can you propose minimal redlines for Annex A that balance procurement's ask and our operational needs (especially the submenu on further subcontracting and audit rights)? Jordan — I'll need a procurement checklist we can share with EdgeHarbor.

I'll set a tentative follow-up for Tuesday to surface the annex draft.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Torres <michael@edgeharbor.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request to add EdgeHarbor CDN as subprocessor (DPA Annex draft + evidence)

Karthik / Jordan —

I reviewed the factsheet. Drafting notes and negotiation posture below (high level):

1) Annex A (subprocessor flow-down)
- Require: mirror DPA obligations (confidentiality, purpose limitation, deletion/return, security measures, assistance with data subject requests).
- Further subcontracting: propose Redwood language: "Subprocessor shall not engage another subprocessor for access to Customer Data without Redwood's prior written consent, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld. Subprocessor may engage Sub-subprocessors for non-confidential infrastructure services upon 30 days' prior notice, unless Redwood objects for reasonable grounds."
- Audit rights: operational attestation annually + right to request evidence (SOC 2 or equivalent) on an exceptions basis. We should avoid broad on-site audit rights for CDNs due to operational burden.

2) Evidence pack (what we can accept)
- Current SOC 2 Type II report or SOC 2 bridge letter (last 12 months).
- Pen test summary (redacted executive summary).
- Encryption-in-transit details (TLS version, cipher suites).
- Data segregation statement: whether EdgeHarbor can segregate caches by customer or if cache key includes an opaque customer token.

3) Contract mechanics and timeline
- We can offer a limited Annex A with a 12-month review clause and a 60-day opt-out if a material incident occurs. This gives procurement some assurance and gives us operational flexibility.
- DocuSign flow: we can issue Annex A as an attachment to the order form (no MSA amendment needed if Annex A is accepted).

Jordan: please pull an evidence checklist and confirm who on procurement will accept the SOC2 bridge vs full report. If they insist on on-site audits, we need to escalate.

Karthik: draft messaging to EdgeHarbor that includes the proposed Annex summary and the evidence checklist. Keep tone collaborative — procurement are close to their deadline.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Michael Torres <michael@edgeharbor.com>

Subject: Re: Request to add EdgeHarbor CDN as subprocessor (next steps + annex summary)

Hi Michael —

Thanks for sending the factsheet — that's helpful. Kimberly and I discussed and here's the proposed path to meet procurement's 12/15 target: 

1) Evidence pack (please provide by 11/30):
   - SOC 2 Type II report OR SOC 2 bridge letter covering last 12 months
   - Redacted pen test executive summary
   - TLS/encryption config note (TLS 1.2+; preferred 1.3)
   - Short note on cache segregation (how keys are scoped)
   - Primary security contact (name/email)

2) Annex A summary (attached as redline): key points
   - Flow-down of DPA obligations for EU data (confidentiality, limited use, deletion)
   - Subcontracting: prior written consent for any subprocessor that would access unredacted customer content; notice + 30-day objection for infrastructure sub-subprocessors
   - Audit: accept annual SOC 2 or attestation; targeted evidence requests permitted on exception
   - 12-month review clause and 60-day incident opt-out (gives procurement rollback path)

3) Execution plan
   - You provide evidence pack by 11/30
   - Kimberly will issue Annex A redline by 11/24; once agreed we'll route via DocuSign as an Annex to the order form
   - Jordan will coordinate billing/PO references and confirm procurement's DocuSign signatory

If that timeline works, I'll open the DocuSign envelope and we can get this across the finish line before 12/15. If procurement needs stricter subcontracting language, flag now so Kimberly can advise on escalation.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
